newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister clears way for probe of Gaullists.
newsitem.headline: French minister clears way for probe of Gaullists.

text.p: French Justice Minister Elisabeth Guigou pledged on Monday not to intervene in a sleaze probe targetting top officials of President Jacques Chirac's Gaullist Rally for the Republic (RPR) party.
Guigou, who took office earlier this month after the Left ousted the RPR in parliamentary elections, said she had told public prosecutors justice must take its course.

In a series of interviews and a written statement, Guigou singled out the case, centring on suspicions that the RPR was financed by systematic kickbacks on Paris regional housing authority tenders, as an example of her new hands-off policy.
The probe could topple Paris mayor Jean Tiberi, a long-time ally of Chirac who succeeded him at city hall after Chirac's election as president in 1995.
"In corruption scandals, political leaders gave the impression, often justified, that they tried to interfere to bury investigations," she told Le Monde.
"I want a radical break with the system I discovered when I took office. In principle there is no interference, but in reality there is interference by telephone in the most total secrecy," she said.
"I want no more of that (and) I will demonstrate this in specific cases, particularly in the case being investigated by Judge Halphen," she said, referring to to the magistrate leading the probe.

Halphen has become the scourge of the RPR both because of the probe, and a separate investigation he tried to launch into suspicions that Tiberi had the Paris municipality refurbish a city-owned flat for his son.
Tiberi chaired the city housing authority when the controversial renovation occurred in 1988.
